profiles.meeting_scenario: An internal planning meeting at a global investment bank to define a 12-week pilot for adopting Rough Martingale Optimal Transport (RMOT) as an FRTB methodology for non-modelable risk factors in the equity exotics business. The context is the upcoming annual capital planning cycle: the quant team has a research prototype showing finite extrapolation bounds and large apparent capital relief, and the regulatory program office wants to decide what must be built, documented, and reviewed before taking it to the model risk committee and the FRTB steering committee. The agenda is to align on pilot scope, deliverables, owners, supporting data, governance steps, and timing. The expected outcome is a shared plan for what the 'pilot' includes, what evidence will be shown, how the capital benefit will be presented, and what needs to be ready for a September review slot.

members.name: Dr. Elena Park
members.role: Head of Quantitative Methodology, Equity Derivatives
members.expertise: Stochastic volatility, model calibration, pricing bounds, and quantitative research translation into trading methodologies
members.background: Former sell-side derivatives quant and academic researcher who joined the bank three years ago to lead advanced methodology work for exotic derivatives and market risk capital models.
members.private_state: She wants to protect the methodological integrity of the RMOT framework, avoid committing to a broader implementation than her small team can support this quarter, and secure a governance pathway without turning the pilot into a full production build prematurely.
hidden_assumptions: When senior stakeholders ask for a 'pilot,' they usually mean a representative proof on one equity exotics sample book that demonstrates methodological viability rather than a desk-wide operational rollout.

When people say 'validated on live SPX/NDX data,' they mean replaying official historical market snapshots inside the research stack, because the key question is whether the methodology behaves correctly on real market observations, not whether production data plumbing is complete.
A 'capital relief' figure should be stated against the classical MOT benchmark used in the research memo, before downstream overlays, reserves, or management adjustments are added.
A September model risk review can be tentatively secured with a methodology note, numerical evidence, and a roadmap, with implementation details and controls filled in afterward.

members.name: Daniel Ruiz
members.expertise: FRTB implementation, governance workflows, model risk submissions, and coordination across Risk, Finance, and front-office technology
members.background: Previously managed the bank's standardized approach remediation program and now oversees delivery plans for market risk capital changes that must withstand audit, model validation, and regulatory challenge.
members.private_state: He wants a plan that can survive governance scrutiny, fit the annual budget and capital timeline, and avoid a late-stage surprise where a promising research result cannot be used because traceability, controls, or submission standards were assumed rather than delivered.
hidden_assumptions: When the steering committee approves a 'pilot,' they expect something broad enough to be reused for the full equity NMRF population, including governance artefacts and a path to operational adoption.
When people say 'live data,' they mean production-sourced end-of-day market data and official valuation extracts that Finance and Risk can trace back to the bank's controlled feeds.
A 'capital relief' number only counts as decision-grade if it is measured against the current internal capital number seen by Finance leadership after overlays and existing governance adjustments.

A September model risk review date is only real if the full submission pack, reproducible test evidence, implementation notes, and control attestations are circulated by the cutoff before the meeting.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to 'the pilot' as if it were a single agreed package.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 thinks the pilot is a representative proof-of-concept on a sampled equity exotics book, likely centered on autocallables and selected NMRFs, sufficient to demonstrate RMOT methodology and indicative impact.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 thinks the pilot should cover the operationally relevant equity NMRF population, or at least be packaged so it can stand in for a desk-wide governance pilot rather than a narrow research exercise.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In business planning meetings, 'pilot' is a routine word that feels self-explanatory; both parties expect later workstreams to fill in details, so neither pauses to define the exact coverage boundary.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say the framework has to be shown on 'live SPX/NDX data.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of replaying actual prior-day or historical official market snapshots for SPX and NDX options inside the quant research environment.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of current controlled production end-of-day feeds and official marks, with traceable lineage suitable for governance and audit.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are indeed referring to real SPX/NDX market data rather than synthetic data, so the phrase sounds aligned; the divergence sits in which exact data instance and environment qualifies as 'live.'

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both discuss producing a 'capital relief' number for the steering deck.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 intends to report the reduction relative to the classical MOT benchmark in the research setup, before overlays, reserves, and managerial adjustments, because that isolates the methodological contribution of RMOT.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 expects a number relative to the currently reported internal capital view after existing overlays and governance adjustments, because that is what senior management treats as realizable relief.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are using standard finance language and both expect the number to be conservative and business-relevant; the hidden gap is the unstated criterion for what counts as the baseline.

misalignment_points.topic: What it means to be ready for September review
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both talk about being 'ready for the September model risk review.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 presupposes that being ready means having the methodology paper, empirical results, and a clear implementation roadmap in hand so that the committee can review the concept and request follow-ups.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 presupposes that being ready means a near-complete submission pack is already assembled before the cutoff, including testing evidence, controlled inputs, implementation notes, and attestations from supporting teams.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Calendar-based readiness language is common in governance planning, and both participants are accustomed to saying a review is 'in September' without restating the hidden submission prerequisites every time.

If we can lock the methodology, empirical evidence, and a sensible roadmap, that should be enough to be ready for the September model risk review. The governance path can mature afterward.
